refresh_datasource.description: Rebuild a published data source's extract and wait for it to finish. Tableau only *queues* a refresh when asked, so this follows the job to completion and fails if the rebuild failed - a refresh that cannot reach the underlying data still starts cleanly and reports the failure only on the job afterwards. The data source has to have an extract; a live connection queries its source directly and has nothing to rebuild.
refresh_datasource.display_str_template: Refresh a Tableau data source extract.
refresh_datasource.name: refresh_datasource

parameters.description: The published data source's Tableau id (a GUID). List data sources returns it.
parameters.name: datasource_id

parameters.description: Keep the step running until Tableau reports the extract rebuilt, and fail if it did not. Turn this off only if you want to start the refresh and follow it yourself with Get a job - Tableau accepts the request and answers with a queued job either way, so with this off the step cannot tell you whether the rebuild worked.
parameters.display_name: Wait for the refresh to finish
parameters.name: wait_for_completion

parameters.description: How long to wait for the rebuild before returning. A big extract can take longer than this; if it does, the result comes back with 'timed_out' set and the refresh carries on in Tableau - follow it with Get a job.
parameters.name: timeout_seconds

refresh_datasource.result_str_template: Extract refresh job {tableau_refresh_datasource,id} finished with code {tableau_refresh_datasource,finish_code}.
